answer: Among black females in the NLS 1979 cohort (n=1,548), the largest adjacent-wave increase in median composite wealth occurred between 1985 and 1990, when the median rose from $175 to $2,600 (+$2,425), exceeding the 1990–1996 change of +$1,400; the cumulative 1985–1996 change of +$3,825 is reported only as a secondary diagnostic spanning the two adjacent intervals.

payload.hypothesis: Among black females in the NLS 1979 cohort (n=1,548), the largest adjacent-wave increase in median composite wealth occurred between 1985 and 1990, when the median rose from $175 to $2,600 (+$2,425), exceeding the 1990–1996 change of +$1,400; the cumulative 1985–1996 change of +$3,825 is noted only as a secondary diagnostic spanning the two adjacent intervals.
payload.workflow: Loaded data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013 rows, 6 cols, zero missingness across all columns). Filtered to race=='black' AND sex=='female' (n=1,548; per-year valid N=1,548 for all three wealth columns). Kept negative and zero composite wealth values (NLS debt convention). Computed raw medians at each wave: 1985=$175, 1990=$2,600, 1996=$4,000. Computed three pairwise median differences — adjacent: Δ(1990−1985)=+$2,425, Δ(1996−1990)=+$1,400; full-span diagnostic: Δ(1996−1985)=+$3,825. Identified the largest adjacent-wave increase as 1985→1990. Robustness footnote: BF raw means are 1985=$10,646.94, 1990=$24,496.24, 1996=$42,691.89, under which the largest adjacent increase flips to 1990→1996 (mean Δ +$18,195.65 vs +$13,849.30); the median-led hypothesis is unchanged. No bootstrap CI, no winsorisation, no log-transform, no re-derivation of the composite.
